messages:
jamie: Heads up, control-plane telemetry is leaking tenant IPs into traces through peered links. Can we design a minimal pattern to keep per-endpoint metrics without PII?

marta: Two immediate options: (A) tiny local telemetry proxy/agent in customer VPC that scrubs/redacts IPs and emits only hashed tenant + service labels, or (B) do redaction/sampling at our regional gateway and attach coarse route labels there.

devin: Agent approach is best privacy-wise but we cant require it for cross-account peering or customers who won't run agents. Gateway approach centralizes ops but increases risk of PII in logs if were not careful.

lina: For the agent, enforce output labels: ["tenant_hash", "svc_qualifier", "region", "session_opaque_id"]. No src/dst IPs, no port numbers. Keep traces aggregated. :shield:

kevin: svc_qualifier derivation is tricky. Relying on SNI can fail (corporate proxies rewrite SNI). We should support ALPN + explicit agent header fallback.

marta: Agree. Agent emits svc_qualifier, but gateway path can infer from ALPN/port mapping and fall back to route hash when missing.

jamie: Ops wants per-endpoint latency histograms for SLA investigations, but without exposing tenant IPs. That suggests an ephemeral session id that ties requests for a short TTL.

devin: Proposed: cp-telemetry-agent registers session via a short mTLS call to control plane, gets back session_id token. Metrics include session_id + tenant_hash + svc_qualifier. No IPs.

lina: Control plane stores session_id -> metadata for TTL seconds and purges after expiry. We can join histograms to traces only within retention window.

kevin: How about cross-account peering where we cant run agents in customer accounts?

marta: Two options there: eBPF/redaction on our gateway to strip IPs and attach inferred route_hash, or a token exchange where customer side proactively registers expected connections to get telemetry tokens.

jamie: Token exchange sketch: customer-side micro-RPC (mTLS) that asks CP for a telemetry_token for upcoming conn_id. Gateway inspects connection metadata and adds telemetry_token label to emitted metrics.

devin: Avoid placing token in TLS internals. Use separate small mTLS RPC over controlchannel at session open. Example: POST /v1/register {conn_id, svc, ttl} -> {telemetry_token, expires_at}.

kevin: Token store needs to be low-latency and replicated regionally. Expect token QPS correlated with connection churn. We'll measure in spike.

marta: Edge cases: shared NATs mean many tenants from same IP. Tokens disambiguate. Also require customer opt-in for token-based attribution; default is to treat unknown source as "unattributed" and sample.

ops-bot: Security/compliance reminder: log redaction and ephemeral identifier design require COMP-2026 ticket.

jamie: Immediate proposal: run a two-path spike this sprint. Sidecar/agent prototype (owner: @lina, 2d) and gateway token-exchange prototype (owner: @devin, 3d). Measure extra latency, token-store QPS, and failure modes.

lina: Ill do a minimal Go agent that does hashed tenant id + session registration, and a prom push to a sandbox metrics cluster.

devin: Ill implement a gateway shim that accepts telemetry_token header on connection metadata and consults a memcached-style store to resolve tenant labels; will measure 99th p99 add-on latency.

kevin: Also write a short doc section listing default redactions (IP, port, full path) and fallback label derivation (ALPN, port map, explicit header).

marta: After spikes, present results in arch sync and decide. :white_check_mark:
